You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Continual-ARC task-e4f7b624. Uniform-background grid has equal-length same-color segments on opposite edges (vertical bars left/right or horizontal bars top/bottom), shifted along the edge; sparse markers of a second color are aligned with one segment. For each marker, extend a straight line of its original color from the associated segment up to (but not overwriting) the marker, then change the marker to 4. Transfer the marker's offset within that segment to the opposite segment and extend a straight ray inward from the opposite border all the way across to the opposite grid edge, including that edge's background cells; preserve the border segments themselves. Only transferred offsets are filled, not every row/column in the edge bands. Match offsets from segment starts, not mirrored offsets. Orientation applies equally to vertical and horizontal segment pairs.

Confirmed demo (18x24, bg3, boundary color1, marker color5): top bar r0,c0-6; bottom bar r17,c14-20. Markers (r9,c14),(r13,c15),(r13,c16),(r14,c20),(r15,c18). Markers become 4 and source rays extend downward to row16. Their offsets from bottom-bar start c14 map to top bar at c0,c1,c2,c6,c4; each mapped column is filled with 5 from r1 through r16, preserving both boundary bars.

Confirmed solved test (21x27, bg8, bar color9): left bar c0,r4-11; right bar c26,r13-20. Markers color3 in left band: (4,17),(6,21),(7,2),(9,22),(10,5),(11,17). Each marker became 4; fill color3 leftward from c1 through the cell before its marker. Transfer each row offset r-4 to right band row r+9 and fill c0-25 color3, preserving c26=9.

New confirmed horizontal demo (26x23, bg5, boundary 8): top bar r0,c4-7; bottom bar r25,c0-3; markers color3 at (r3,c4),(r4,c5). Markers become 4; source rays fill down from top bar to just before each marker. Offsets 0,1 transfer to bottom columns c0,c1, filled all the way up through row0 while the bottom bar stays 8. This confirms the opposite-border ray reaches the far grid edge, not merely the interior rows.

New solved test (5x17, bg9, boundary 6): top bar r0,c0-7; bottom bar r4,c9-16; markers color1 at r2,c2-4,c7 and r3,c0,c1,c6. Source rays fill downward from top bar to markers; markers become4. Offsets 0,1,2,3,4,6,7 transfer to bottom columns c9,10,11,12,13,15,16, with rays filled all the way to row0 (overwriting bg in row0 at those columns). The first attempt missed these opposite-ray endpoints on row0; correction yielded the exact solution.
